Congress can restore thousands in earned benefits to more than 50,000 veterans this week. Here’s how we get it done. 👇🏼🧵
The Major Richard Star Act has been introduced in each of the last four Congresses.
In the last three congresses, the bill had more than 300 cosponsors in the House. In this Congress, it has 342 cosponsors in the House and 80 in the Senate.

Right now, more than 59,000 veterans who were injured in combat and forced to retire early aren’t getting their full military retirement pay because they also receive VA disability benefits. This needs to change.

Even with a ton of support, the bill has never been voted on. In May, @RepMarkTakano decided to file a discharge petition to force a vote on the House floor. To succeed, a discharge petition needs 218 signatures from House members.
A few Republicans finally joined us, and in September, we reached the 218 signatures needed to force a vote.
After years of waiting, the House is finally voting on the Major Richard Star Act this week.

If it passes, combat-injured veterans will receive both their full military retirement pay and VA disability benefits. That means an average of $1,200 more a month for veterans who have already sacrificed so much for us.
Congress must pass the Major Richard Star Act. It’s long past time to get our veterans the full benefits they deserve.

🧵: High energy costs are a top concern for families in Texas and across our country. As a representative of the energy capital of the world, I've been working for years to fix the broken permitting system driving up costs and delaying progress. The Bipartisan American

New power generation, power lines, or other energy infrastructure often require federal approval. The most complex reviews take nearly four years on average, and court reviews of even good projects can take up to six years after that. Those delays add costs that are passed on to

If enacted, BAAJA would speed up approvals for new power plants and power lines while maintaining safeguards for clean air and clean water. Getting more power on the grid sooner means lower costs for families. (3/8)

BAAJA would also help bring more renewable energy online. Renewables make up 83% of the power waiting to connect to the grid today, and BAAJA would protect approved projects from political interference, so that developers can build them and no administration can cancel them on a

The bill also holds data centers accountable. If a new data center requires new power lines or grid upgrades, the data center must pay the full cost. Families should not have to subsidize the electricity costs of some of the largest technology companies in the world. (5/8)

Independent analyses of the original bill found that BAAJA could save households up to $78 a year on their electricity bills by 2040 and cut carbon emissions from power plants by about 1.8 billion tons through 2041. (6/8)

Any bipartisan agreement requires trade-offs, and BAAJA is not perfect. But it is the best opportunity we have had in years to take meaningful action on energy costs and to build the infrastructure we need. We should not miss it. (7/8)

The Senate leaders have released an updated version of the bill, and I will review its changes closely. I look forward to working with my colleagues to pass permitting reform and to deliver relief to Texans and all Americans. (8/8)
